testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-001
testCases.input: How many days of annual leave does a full-time employee with less than 3 years' service receive?
testCases.actualOutput: A full-time employee with less than 3 years’ service receives 27 days of annual leave, plus 8 bank holidays (35 paid days off in total per leave year).
testCases.expectedOutput: A full-time employee with less than 3 years' continuous service receives 27 days of annual leave plus the 8 England and Wales bank holidays, a total of 35 paid days off per leave year (262.5 hours).
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.1 Annual leave entitlement

**Table 6.1 — Annual leave entitlement for full-time employees (37.5 hours per week, 5 days per week)**

|**Continuous service completed**|**Annual leave (days)**|**Bank holidays (days)**|**Total paid days off per leave**|
|---|---|---|---|
||||**year**|
|Less than 3 years|27|8|35|
|3 years or more, but less than 5 years|28|8|36|
|5 years or more|29|8|37|

- One day of annual leave equals **7.5 hours** for a full-time employee.

- The service-related increase applies from the **first 1 January that falls after** the date on which the employee completes the required continuous service. It is not applied part-way through a leave year.

- The entitlement applies to permanent and fixed-term employees, apprentices and interns. Part-time employees receive a pro-rated entitlement calculated in hours (section 6.3).

- Contractors and agency workers do not receive Northstar annual leave; agency workers' holiday is provided through their agency.

### **Statutory minimum holiday**

Almost all workers are legally entitled to 5.6 weeks' paid holiday per year, capped at 28 days for someone working 5 or more days a week. Employers may include bank holidays within the 5.6 weeks. Northstar's entitlement of 27 days plus 8 bank holidays (35 days for a full-time employee) exceeds the statutory minimum. No pro-rating or rounding rule in this handbook will ever reduce an employee's entitlement below the statutory minimum.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.1 Entitlement **Table 3.1 — Annual leave entitlement (full-time, 37.5 hours over 5 days)** |**Continuous service completed**|**Annual leave**
**days**|**Bank holidays**|**Total days**|**Total hours**| |---|---|---|---|---| |Less than 3 years|27|8|35|262.5| |3 years or more, less than 5 years|28|8|36|270.0| |5 years or more|29|8|37|277.5| Service increments apply from the first 1 January that falls after the employee completes the required service. ### **Service increment timing** - Start date 15 March 2024: 3 years completed on 14 March 2027. The first 1 January after that is 1 January 2028, so the employee receives 28 days from the 2028 leave year. In 2027 the entitlement remains 27 days. - Start date 1 January 2024: 3 years completed at the end of 31 December 2026. The first 1 January after that is 1 January 2027, so the employee receives 28 days in the 2027 leave year.

testCases.input: What is the deadline for reporting sickness absence on the first day?
testCases.actualOutput: Call your line manager by 09:30 on the first day. If you work shifts or are on call, call at least 1 hour before your shift or rota period starts.
testCases.expectedOutput: Employees must call their line manager by telephone or Teams call no later than 09:30 on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least 1 hour before their shift or rota period starts. The absence must also be recorded in PeopleHub the same day.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

the shift or rota period.| |Channel|Telephone or Teams call to the line manager (Head of Department or team lead if
unavailable). Text, chat or email alone is not sufficient unless the employee is
physically unable to speak.| |Record|Absence recorded in PeopleHub the same day by the employee or manager.| |Updates|On the third working day, then at least weekly.| |Return|Self-certification on return; return-to-work conversation within 2 working days.|

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-003
testCases.input: What is the deadline for submitting an expense claim?
testCases.actualOutput:
Submit your claim within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred.

- For a multi-day trip, submit all expenses together within 30 calendar days of the trip’s first expense.
- Claims submitted 31–90 days later need a written explanation and Head of Department approval; claims submitted more than 90 days later are not reimbursed unless the Finance Director approves an exception.
- If you are leaving Northstar, submit all claims within 10 working days after your leaving date.
testCases.expectedOutput: Expense claims must be submitted in ExpenseFlow within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred. Claims 31 to 90 days late need a written explanation and Head of Department approval; claims more than 90 days late are not reimbursed without a Finance Director exception.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Submission deadlines

### **Deadlines**

- Submit within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. For multi-day trips, each expense's own date applies, but all expenses for one trip should be submitted together within 30 calendar days of the first expense of the trip.

- **31 to 90 calendar days:** a late claim requires a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- **More than 90 calendar days:** not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the claimant was on long-term sickness or family leave).

- **Leavers:** all claims must be submitted within **10 working days** after the leaving date. Claims received after that are not paid.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-011
testCases.input: How many statutory flexible-working requests can an employee make in a year?
testCases.actualOutput: An employee can make up to 2 statutory flexible-working requests in any 12-month period.
testCases.expectedOutput: All employees can make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment and can make up to 2 statutory requests in any 12-month period.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.6 Formal flexible-working requests

All employees can make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and can make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . A request can cover hours, start and finish times, working days, or place of work.

## **Flexible working — process and deadlines**

1. Submit a written request in PeopleHub stating that it is a statutory request for flexible working, the date of the request, the working pattern requested and the proposed start date, and whether and when any earlier request was made. 2. The line manager acknowledges the request within **5 working days** . 3. The line manager meets the employee to discuss the request within **4 weeks** of receiving it. A request cannot be refused without first consulting the employee. 4. A written decision is issued, and any appeal concluded, within **2 months** of the date of the request, unless the employee agrees to an extension. 5. A refusal must give one or more of the statutory business reasons and explain why it applies. 6. The employee may appeal within **10 working days** of the decision. The appeal is heard by a different, more senior manager.

The statutory business reasons for refusing a request are: the burden of additional costs; inability to reorganise work among existing staff; inability to recruit additional staff; a detrimental effect on quality; a detrimental effect on performance; a detrimental effect on ability to meet customer demand; insufficient work during the periods the employee proposes to work; and planned structural changes. Managers may agree a **trial period of up to 3 months** before confirming a permanent change.

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
5 Formal flexible-working requests > 5.1 Eligibility

Every employee may make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and may make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . Contractors and agency workers cannot use this procedure.

testCases.input: My kid's nursery shut out of the blue today — what time off can I take?
testCases.actualOutput: You can take a reasonable amount of time off to deal with the unexpected nursery closure and arrange alternative care. Northstar pays up to 2 working days for this occurrence, subject to a maximum of 5 paid days in the leave year; any further time is unpaid or you can use annual leave.
testCases.expectedOutput: This is an emergency involving a dependant, covered by the statutory right to a reasonable amount of time off for dependants (unpaid by law, from day one). Northstar pays up to 2 working days per occurrence, up to 5 paid days per leave year; further time is unpaid or you may use annual leave. Call your line manager as soon as possible.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.8 Time off for dependants, emergency leave and carer's leave

**Time off for dependants (statutory).** All employees may take a reasonable amount of time off to deal with an emergency involving a dependant — for example, a child falling ill, a breakdown in care arrangements, or a dependant being involved in an incident. A dependant can be a spouse, partner, child, grandchild, parent, or someone who depends on the employee for care. The right covers unexpected situations, not events the employee knew about in advance. There is no fixed limit; "reasonable" usually means enough time to deal with the immediate emergency and arrange alternative care. Statutory time off for dependants is unpaid.

**Northstar enhancement.** Northstar pays up to **2 working days per occurrence** , up to a maximum of **5 paid days per leave year** . Further time is unpaid, or the employee may choose to use annual leave.

**Carer's leave (statutory).** Employees can take up to **one week** of unpaid carer's leave in any 12-month period to give or arrange care for a dependant with a long-term care need. It is available from the first day of employment and can be taken in half days, individual days or a whole week. Notice must be at least 3 days for a half day or a full day, and at least twice the length of the leave for more than one day. No evidence of the dependant's care needs is required. **Northstar enhancement:** the first **3 days** of carer's leave in any rolling 12 months are paid at full basic pay.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-025
testCases.input: I'm in month 4 of my probation and was off sick for 4 days. Will I get company sick pay?
testCases.actualOutput: No. During probation, your entitlement is SSP only, not company sick pay. SSP is payable from the first day of sickness if you meet the statutory conditions.
testCases.expectedOutput: Company sick pay depends on service: during probation the entitlement is SSP only. Since 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness at the lower of £123.25 a week or 80% of normal weekly earnings, provided statutory conditions are met. You must have followed the reporting and self-certification rules.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.4 Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)

## **Statutory Sick Pay from 6 April 2026**

Following the Employment Rights Act 2025, from 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness absence (the former 3 unpaid "waiting days" were removed) and the lower earnings limit no longer applies to eligibility. The weekly rate is £123.25 or 80% of the employee's normal weekly earnings, whichever is lower, for up to 28 weeks. Northstar's qualifying days for SSP are the employee's contracted working days. SSP rates are set by government and usually change each April.

An employee who is the biological father of the child, or the partner of the mother or adopter, and who expects to have responsibility for the child's upbringing, may take up to **2 weeks** of paternity leave, as one 2-week block or two separate 1-week blocks. Leave cannot start before the birth and must end within 52 weeks of the birth (or of the due date if the baby is born early).

**Notice.** The employee must tell People Operations the due date at least 15 weeks before the baby is due, and must give 28 days' notice to change the start date of paternity leave.

**Statutory Paternity Pay.** SPP is £194.32 per week or 90% of AWE, whichever is lower. It requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the qualifying week (the 15th week before the EWC), continued employment up to the date of birth, and AWE of at least £129.

**Northstar enhancement.** Employees who qualify for SPP receive **full basic pay for 2 weeks** , inclusive of SPP. Employees who are entitled to paternity leave but do not qualify for SPP (for example, because they joined less than 26 weeks before the qualifying week) take paternity leave unpaid; they may choose to use annual leave instead for some or all of the period.

## **Work From Abroad examples**

- **Within the limit:** An employee who has not worked abroad in the past 12 months requests to work from Portugal for 5 working days in July 2027, submitting the request 6 weeks ahead. Approvable, subject to all three approvals.

- **Rolling limit exceeded:** An employee worked abroad for 6 days in February 2027 and asks for 5 days in October 2027. Within the rolling 12 months this would total 11 days, so only **4 days** can be approved unless the Director of People Operations approves an exception (maximum 20 days).

- **Restricted customer data:** An employee who supports a customer's payroll platform (Restricted data) asks to work from Italy for a week. testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-029
testCases.input: What conditions must I meet to get Northstar's enhanced maternity pay, and what does it pay?
testCases.actualOutput:
You must qualify for Statutory Maternity Pay and have at least 26 weeks’ continuous service at the end of the 15th week before your expected week of childbirth (EWC).

- Weeks 1–16: full basic pay, inclusive of SMP.
- Weeks 17–39: SMP only.
- Weeks 40–52: unpaid.
testCases.expectedOutput: Enhanced maternity pay requires that you qualify for SMP (including average weekly earnings of at least £129) and have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth. It pays full basic pay (inclusive of SMP) for weeks 1–16, SMP only for weeks 17–39, and nothing for weeks 40–52. If you do not return for at least 6 months after maternity leave, the enhanced element above SMP is repayable, except for redundancy, ill-health capability or a further immediately following period of statutory family leave. Maternity leave itself (52 weeks) is a day-one right.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.1 Maternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Pregnant employees are entitled to up to 52 weeks of Statutory Maternity Leave (26 weeks of Ordinary Maternity Leave and 26 weeks of Additional Maternity Leave), regardless of length of service, hours or pay. The earliest leave can start is 11 weeks before the EWC. Employees must take at least 2 weeks of compulsory maternity leave after the birth.

**Notice.** By the end of the 15th week before the EWC, the employee must tell People Operations (via PeopleHub) that she is pregnant, her EWC and the date she wants maternity leave to start. Northstar will confirm the expected return date in writing within 28 days. To change the return date, the employee must give at least 8 weeks' notice.

**Statutory Maternity Pay.** SMP requires at least 28 days' notice of the date SMP should start and evidence of pregnancy (a MATB1 certificate or a letter from a doctor or midwife) within 21 days of the SMP start date. A MATB1 cannot be issued more than 20 weeks before the due date. Employees who do not qualify for SMP may be able to claim Maternity Allowance from the government; Northstar will issue form SMP1 explaining why SMP is not payable.

**Northstar enhanced maternity pay.** Employees who qualify for SMP **and** have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the EWC receive:

**Table 8.1 — Northstar enhanced maternity and adoption pay**

|**Weeks of leave**|**Payment**|
|---|---|
|Weeks 1 to 16|Full basic pay, inclusive of SMP or SAP.|
|Weeks 17 to 39|SMP or SAP only.|
|Weeks 40 to 52|Unpaid.|

If the employee does not return to work for at least **6 months** after the end of maternity leave, she must repay the enhanced element (the amount paid above SMP), unless employment ends because of redundancy, ill-health capability, or a further period of statutory family leave immediately following the first. Statutory pay is never repayable because an employee does not return.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-039
testCases.input: I'm a G2 engineer and I've just resigned. I have 5 days of approved leave booked for after my last day. What happens?
testCases.actualOutput: Your 5 days of approved leave after your leaving date are automatically cancelled.
testCases.expectedOutput: As a G2 after probation your contractual notice is 1 month. Approved leave that falls after your leaving date is cancelled automatically. Your final holiday balance is the pro-rated entitlement to the leaving date plus valid carryover minus leave taken or booked; positive balances are paid at annual basic salary / 260 per day, and over-taken leave is deducted where the contract permits. You may ask to take leave during your notice period, and Northstar may require you to take accrued leave during notice by giving notice of at least twice the length of that leave. Final adjustments are paid per the final pay timing rule (section 22.11).
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.16 Leave during probation, negative balances and leave during notice periods

**Probation.** During probation an employee may book leave that will have accrued by the first day of the leave (the annual entitlement x complete calendar months of service / 12, rounded up to the nearest 0.5 day) plus up to **2 additional days** with line manager approval. Leave of more than 5 consecutive working days during probation also requires Head of Department approval.

**Negative balances.** After probation, an employee may book their full annual entitlement in advance. With Head of Department approval, an employee may also borrow up to **3 days** from the next leave year in exceptional circumstances. If employment ends when an employee has taken more leave than they have accrued, the excess is deducted from final pay at the daily rate in section 6.17, where the employment contract contains a written deduction clause (all Northstar contracts issued on or after 1 January 2025 contain this clause) or the employee has given prior written consent.

**Notice periods.** Employees serving notice may request leave in the normal way. Northstar may require an employee to take some or all of their accrued but untaken leave during their notice period by giving notice of at least twice the length of the leave to be taken. Approved leave that falls after the employee's leaving date is cancelled automatically. During garden leave (section 22.6), Northstar may require accrued leave to be taken.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.4 Notice periods **Table 22.4 — Notice periods** |**Situation**|**Notice the employee must give (contractual)**|**Notice Northstar must give**| |---|---|---| |During probation|1 week|1 week| |After probation, grades G1 to G3|1 month|The greater of 1 month and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G4 and G5|2 months|The greater of 2 months and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G6 and G7|3 months|The greater of 3 months and the statutory
minimum| ## **Statutory minimum notice** An employee with more than 1 month's service must give at least 1 week's notice. An employer must give at least 1 week's notice to an employee with between 1 month and 2 years' service, then 1 week for each complete year of service from 2 years, up to a maximum of 12 weeks after 12 years. A contract can give more than these minimums but never less. Notice periods in Table 22.4 are illustrative Northstar contractual terms; the individual employment contract prevails. **Example.** Northstar gives notice to a G2 engineer with 9 complete years of service. Contractual notice is 1 month; statutory notice is 9 weeks. Northstar must give **9 weeks** ' notice because it is longer. If the same engineer resigns, they need give only their contractual notice of 1 month.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-040
testCases.input: Can I take 3 days off during a customer go-live that my Head of Department has published as a critical delivery period?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes, but only exceptionally: leave during the published critical delivery period needs both your line manager’s and Head of Department’s approval, and is not guaranteed. For 3 working days, submit the request in PeopleHub at least 10 working days before the first day of leave; it must show as “Approved” before you take it.
testCases.expectedOutput: Critical delivery periods must be published at least 6 weeks ahead, last at most 15 working days and no more than 2 per team per year. Leave within one requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval and is normally approved only in exceptional circumstances (for example, a family wedding booked before publication). The normal 10-working-day notice for 2–5 days still applies. Leave approved before publication remains approved and can only be cancelled by the company in exceptional circumstances with re-credit and reimbursement of evidenced non-refundable costs.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.7 Manager response, team coverage and critical delivery periods

- Managers must approve or decline a request in PeopleHub within **5 working days** of submission. If there is no decision after 5 working days, PeopleHub automatically escalates the request to the Head of Department. A request is not approved by default because a manager did not respond.

- Unless the Head of Department approves otherwise, no more than **30% of a team** (rounded down, with a minimum of one person) may be on planned annual leave on the same working day. For a team of 8 this is 2 people; for a team of 3 it is 1 person.

- A Head of Department may designate a **critical delivery period** (for example, a customer go-live, a data-centre migration or the Finance year-end close) by publishing it in PeopleHub at least **6 weeks** before it starts. A critical delivery period may last no more than **15 working days** , and no team may have more than **2** critical delivery periods in a leave year.

- Annual leave requested for dates within a published critical delivery period requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval, and will normally be approved only in exceptional circumstances.

- Leave that was already approved before a critical delivery period was published remains approved. It can only be cancelled by the company under section 6.13.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.6 Requesting leave and minimum notice All annual leave must be requested in PeopleHub and approved before it is taken. Leave is not approved until it shows as "Approved" in PeopleHub. Employees should not book non-refundable travel before approval. **Table 6.6 — Minimum notice for annual leave requests (requests submitted on or after 1 October 2026)** |**Length of leave requested**|**Minimum notice**|**Approver**| |---|---|---| |Up to 1 working day (including hourly and
half-day leave)|2 working days|Line manager| |More than 1 and up to 5 working days|10 working days|Line manager| |More than 5 and up to 10 working days|20 working days|Line manager| |More than 10 and up to 15 consecutive working
days|40 working days|Line manager and Head of Department| |More than 15 consecutive working days|40 working days|Line manager, Head of Department and
Director| **How notice is counted.** Notice is the number of working days between the date the request is submitted in PeopleHub and the first day of leave, counting neither the submission date nor the first day of leave. Bank holidays are not working days. Managers may approve requests made with shorter notice at their discretion where cover allows. Short-notice approval is discretionary and is not an entitlement. Emergency situations are covered by section 9.2 (emergency leave and time off for dependants), not by annual leave rules.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.7 Critical delivery periods and team coverage

A Head of Department may publish a critical delivery period in PeopleHub at least 6 weeks before it starts, lasting no more than 15 working days, with no more than 2 per team per leave year. During that period, annual leave also requires Head of Department approval and is approved only exceptionally (for example, a family wedding booked before the period was published, or compassionate reasons). Leave approved before publication stays approved unless cancelled under handbook section 6.13, with re-credit of the leave and reimbursement of evidenced non-refundable costs.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-041
testCases.input: I'm going from full-time to 22.5 hours (Mon–Wed) on 1 July 2027 and I've already taken 60 hours of leave this year. How is my 2027 leave worked out?
testCases.actualOutput:
Your allowance is calculated separately for each period: full-time, 1 January–30 June, gives 130.171 hours; 22.5 hours (Mon–Wed), 1 July–31 December, gives 79.397 hours. The total is 209.568 hours, rounded up to 209.75 hours.

After deducting 37.5 hours of bank holidays in the first period and 22.5 hours in the second, your bookable annual leave is 149.75 hours. After the 60 hours you’ve taken, 89.75 hours remain from 1 July; 7.5 hours must be reserved for the Wednesday 29 December shutdown day.
testCases.expectedOutput: Under the changed-hours method you split the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded, add them, round up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays falling on working days. Period 1 (1 Jan–30 Jun, 181 days, full-time): 262.5 x 181/365 = 130.171 h. Period 2 (1 Jul–31 Dec, 184 days, 0.6 FTE): 157.5 x 184/365 = 79.397 h. Total 209.568 → 209.75 h. Bank holidays: period 1 has 5 on working days (37.5 h), period 2 has 3 on Mon–Wed (22.5 h). Bookable = 149.75 h; after 60 h taken, 89.75 h remain, of which 7.5 h is reserved for the shutdown day on Wednesday 29 December 2027.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = **149.75 hours**

- If the employee took 60 hours of annual leave in period 1, the remaining balance from 1 July is 149.75 − 60 = **89.75 hours** , of which 7.5 hours must be reserved for the shutdown day that falls on a working day (Wednesday 29 December 2027).

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

## **Worked example 3.4B — part-time to full-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday) from 1 January to 31 March 2027 (90 days), then full-time from 1 April to 31 December 2027 (275 days).

- Period 1: 157.5 x 90 / 365 = 38.836 hours

- Period 2: 262.5 x 275 / 365 = 197.774 hours

- Total: 236.610 hours, rounded up to **236.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days: period 1 (29 Mar) 7.5 hours; period 2 (3 May, 31 May, 30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) 37.5 hours; total 45 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 236.75 − 45 = **191.75 hours**

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours

Part-time employees' entitlement is calculated in hours and includes the bank holiday element, so that part-time employees are treated no less favourably than full-time employees, whichever days they work.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours ## **Part-time entitlement formula** Total annual allowance (hours) = 262.5 hours x (contracted weekly hours / 37.5) 262.5 hours is the full-time total of 35 days (27 annual leave days + 8 bank holidays) x 7.5 hours. For employees with 3 or more years' service the full-time total is 270 hours (36 days); with 5 or more years it is 277.5 hours (37 days). Bank holidays that fall on the employee's normal working days are deducted from the allowance, at the hours the employee would normally have worked that day. The remainder is available to book as annual leave. Rounding: round the total annual allowance up to the nearest 0.25 hour. **Table 6.3 — Part-time allowance examples, 2027 leave year, less than 3 years' service** |**Working pattern**|**FTE**|**Total allowance**
**(hours)**|**Bank holidays on working**
**days in 2027 (hours deducted)**|**Bookable annual leave**

6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours

## **Part-time entitlement formula**

In 2027 the bank holidays in England and Wales fall on Friday 1 January, Friday 26 March, Monday 29 March, Monday 3 May, Monday 31 May, Monday 30 August, Monday 27 December and Tuesday 28 December. An employee working Monday to Wednesday therefore has 6 bank holidays on working days (29 March, 3 May, 31 May, 30 August, 27 December and 28 December).

**Changes to working hours part-way through the leave year.** Where contracted hours change during the leave year, divide the leave year into periods at the date of change. Calculate the allowance for each period as: (annual allowance in hours for that working pattern) x (calendar days in the period / days in the leave year). Add the unrounded results together and then round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour. Deduct bank holidays that fell on working days in each period at the hours worked on that day in that period. Leave already taken in the first period is deducted from the new total. Worked examples are in NDS-HR-LAS-002 section 3.4.

Compressed hours employees (for example, 37.5 hours worked over 4 days) are 1.0 FTE and receive 262.5 hours, with each bank holiday on a working day deducted at the length of that working day (9.375 hours on a 4-day compressed week).

testCases.input: I'm going to Berlin for 3 nights for a customer workshop. What approvals do I need and how do I claim a taxi I paid for in cash euros?
testCases.actualOutput:
Before booking, get Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check for the international trip. If the taxi is a single item costing more than £250, it also needs Line Manager and Head of Department pre-approval.

For the cash taxi fare, claim in pounds using Finance’s published monthly exchange rate for the month you incurred the expense: divide the euro amount by the rate and round to the nearest penny.
testCases.expectedOutput: International travel requires Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check before booking, and an overnight stay is involved. Berlin is Band B: hotel up to £200 per night, breakfast £15, lunch £20, dinner £45, daily meal cap £70, incidental £10 per night. Claims are in sterling: card payments use the statement amount including fees; cash uses Finance's published monthly rate for the month of the expense, sterling = foreign amount / rate rounded to the nearest penny (e.g. €30 / 1.16 = £25.86). Itemised receipts are needed and the claim must be submitted within 30 days; a total over £250 requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-043
testCases.input: I got ill on the second day of my holiday in New York. What should I do to get my leave back?
testCases.actualOutput: Tell your line manager about the sickness as soon as reasonably practicable, because you’re in a different time zone. Provide self-certification if you’re off for up to 7 calendar days, or a fit note if you’re off for more than 7 calendar days; if the requirements are met, the affected holiday days may be reclassified as sickness and credited back to your leave balance.
testCases.expectedOutput: Sickness during annual leave can be reclassified and re-credited if you report it on the first day of sickness by calling your line manager by 09:30, or as soon as reasonably practicable if you are in a different time zone, and provide evidence: self-certification for up to 7 calendar days or a fit note for more than 7. Sickness reported only after you return is not normally reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.12 Sickness during annual leave

An employee who falls ill during annual leave may have the affected days reclassified as sickness absence and re-credited to their annual leave balance, provided that they:

1. report the sickness to their line manager by **09:30** on the first day of sickness (or as soon as reasonably practicable if they are in a different time zone), following section 7.1; and

2. provide self-certification for absences of up to 7 calendar days, or a fit note for absences of more than 7 calendar days, as set out in section 7.3.

Days of sickness reported only after the employee returns from leave will not normally be reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence under section 7.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-044
testCases.input: I'm a remote employee and my last day is Friday 20 November 2026. What are my deadlines for returning equipment and submitting expenses, when is my access cut off, and when will my final holiday pay arrive?
testCases.actualOutput: Return your equipment by Friday 27 November 2026, within 5 working days after your leaving date. Submit expenses by Friday 4 December 2026, within 10 working days after your leaving date. The provided sources don’t specify when your access is cut off; please contact People Operations. Your final holiday-pay adjustment is scheduled for 25 December, but because that date is a bank holiday, expect it on the previous working day, 24 December.
testCases.expectedOutput: Remote or hybrid leavers return equipment within 5 working days after the leaving date: 23–27 November, so by Friday 27 November 2026. Expense claims must be submitted within 10 working days after the leaving date: by Friday 4 December 2026. System and building access is revoked at 17:30 on the last working day. Because the leaving date is after the 10th, November salary is paid as normal on 25 November and final adjustments are paid on the 25th of the following month; 25 December 2026 is Christmas Day (a bank holiday), so payment is on the previous working day, Thursday 24 December 2026.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
20 Company equipment and property > 20.6 Returning equipment

### **Equipment return deadlines**

- **Office-based leavers** return all equipment and their access card to IT on their **last working day** .

- **Remote or hybrid leavers** return all equipment within **5 working days** after their leaving date, using the prepaid courier arranged by IT. Access cards may be posted with the equipment.

- If equipment has not been returned within **10 working days** after the leaving date, IT escalates to People Operations, who send a written reminder and may take recovery action. Any deduction from final pay is made only where the contract permits or the employee has agreed in writing.

- Employees returning from long-term absence or moving role return any equipment no longer needed within 10 working days of IT's request.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.11 Final pay and outstanding annual leave

Salary is paid for the calendar month on the 25th (section 11.1). If the leaving date is **on or before** the 10th of a month, all final pay, including payment for untaken annual leave, approved expenses and any deductions, is paid on the 25th of that month. If the leaving date is **after** the 10th, normal salary for that month is paid on the 25th and the final adjustments (holiday pay, expenses and deductions) are paid on the 25th of the following month. The final holiday balance is calculated as set out in section 6.17.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.1 Salary payment

Salaries are paid monthly, for the calendar month, by bank transfer on the **25th of each month** . If the 25th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, salary is paid on the previous working day.

testCases.input: I've been summoned for jury service during my team's critical delivery period. Do I have to go, and will I be paid?
testCases.actualOutput:
Northstar must allow you time off for jury service. If your absence would seriously harm the business, Northstar may ask you to apply to defer it; jury service can be deferred only once in a 12-month period.

Northstar pays your full basic pay for the first 10 working days of jury service in the leave year. After that, Northstar pay is unpaid, and you may claim loss of earnings from the court.
testCases.expectedOutput: Jury service is a statutory right to time off, not annual leave, so critical-delivery-period rules on annual leave do not apply. Tell your manager and upload the summons within 2 working days. If the absence would seriously harm the business Northstar may ask you to apply to defer, giving you a letter; deferral is possible only once in 12 months. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first 10 working days in a leave year (do not claim loss of earnings for those days); after that it is unpaid and you claim loss of earnings from the court.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Other forms of leave > 9.3 Jury service

Northstar must allow employees time off for jury service. Employees must tell their line manager and upload a copy of the summons to PeopleHub within **2 working days** of receiving it. If the absence would seriously harm the business, Northstar may ask the employee to apply to defer jury service, giving the employee a letter explaining why; jury service can be deferred only once in a 12-month period. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first **10 working days** of jury service in any leave year; the employee must not claim loss of earnings from the court for those days. After 10 working days, jury service is unpaid by Northstar and the employee may claim loss of earnings from the court using the court's employer form, which People Operations will complete.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours ## **Part-time entitlement formula** Total annual allowance (hours) = 262.5 hours x (contracted weekly hours / 37.5) 262.5 hours is the full-time total of 35 days (27 annual leave days + 8 bank holidays) x 7.5 hours. For employees with 3 or more years' service the full-time total is 270 hours (36 days); with 5 or more years it is 277.5 hours (37 days). Bank holidays that fall on the employee's normal working days are deducted from the allowance, at the hours the employee would normally have worked that day. The remainder is available to book as annual leave. An employee working Monday to Wednesday therefore has 6 bank holidays on working days (29 March, 3 May, 31 May, 30 August, 27 December and 28 December).

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours

## **Part-time entitlement formula**

In 2027 the bank holidays in England and Wales fall on Friday 1 January, Friday 26 March, Monday 29 March, Monday 3 May, Monday 31 May, Monday 30 August, Monday 27 December and Tuesday 28 December. An employee working Monday to Wednesday therefore has 6 bank holidays on working days (29 March, 3 May, 31 May, 30 August, 27 December and 28 December).

**Changes to working hours part-way through the leave year.** Where contracted hours change during the leave year, divide the leave year into periods at the date of change. Calculate the allowance for each period as: (annual allowance in hours for that working pattern) x (calendar days in the period / days in the leave year). Add the unrounded results together and then round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour. Deduct bank holidays that fell on working days in each period at the hours worked on that day in that period. Leave already taken in the first period is deducted from the new total. Worked examples are in NDS-HR-LAS-002 section 3.4.

Compressed hours employees (for example, 37.5 hours worked over 4 days) are 1.0 FTE and receive 262.5 hours, with each bank holiday on a working day deducted at the length of that working day (9.375 hours on a 4-day compressed week).

## **Joiner and leaver formula**

Pro-rated annual leave = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / total days in the leave year) Count calendar days inclusive of the start date and the leaving date. The leave year has 365 days (366 in a leap year; 2028 is the next leap year).

Rounding for full-time employees: round up to the nearest 0.5 day. Rounding for part-time employees (hours-based): round up to the nearest 0.25 hour.

Full-time joiners and leavers also receive, as paid days off, the bank holidays that fall during their employment. Part-time joiners and leavers use the hours-based allowance in section 6.3, pro-rated in the same way.

- **Joiner example:** a full-time employee starts on 1 March 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 306 (1 March to 31 December inclusive). 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.64 days, rounded up to **23.0 days** of annual leave, plus the 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027 onwards.

- **Leaver example:** a full-time employee with less than 3 years' service leaves on 30 June 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 181. 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.39 days, rounded up to **13.5 days** .

testCases.input: A full-time employee earning £45,500 leaves on 30 June 2027 having taken 10 days of leave and with no carryover. What holiday pay is due?
testCases.actualOutput: The holiday balance is 3.5 days, so £612.50 gross is due, paid in the final salary payment.
testCases.expectedOutput: Pro-rated entitlement = 27 x 181/365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Daily rate = £45,500 / 260 = £175.00. Payment = 3.5 x £175.00 = £612.50 gross. Because 30 June is after the 10th, it is paid with final adjustments on 25 July 2027.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-056
testCases.input: For a one-night London trip: rail £84, hotel £195 room-only, day 1 lunch £14 and dinner £38 (including a £6 glass of wine), day 2 breakfast £13 and lunch £16, plus the incidental allowance. How much is reimbursed and who approves?
testCases.actualOutput: £342 is reimbursed if the Head of Department approves the £15 hotel excess; otherwise, £327 is reimbursed. The claim needs approval from your line manager and Head of Department, and the Head of Department must approve the hotel exception.
testCases.expectedOutput: Rail £84.00 in full. Hotel capped at the London limit £180.00. Day 1: wine is not reimbursable so dinner is £32.00; lunch £14.00; total £46.00 (under £55 cap). Day 2: breakfast capped at £12.00, lunch capped at £15.00 = £27.00. Incidental £5.00. Total £84 + £180 + £46 + £27 + £5 = £342.00. Claim value £250.01–£1,000 needs line manager and Head of Department approval.
retrievalContext:
Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.1 — two-day London trip**

A Manchester-based consultant travels to London on Tuesday and returns Wednesday, with an approved overnight stay.

- Standard-class return rail: £84.00 — reimbursed in full.

- Hotel: £195.00 room only — limit £180.00; £180.00 reimbursed (the £15.00 excess is not reimbursed unless the Head of Department approves an exception, which is within the 25% threshold).

- Tuesday: lunch £14.00 and dinner £38.00 including a £6.00 glass of wine. Wine is not reimbursable, so dinner = £32.00. Tuesday meals = £46.00 (within the £55 daily cap).

- Wednesday: breakfast £13.00 (limit £12.00) and lunch £16.00 (limit £15.00). Wednesday meals = £27.00.

- Incidental allowance: £5.00.

- **Total reimbursed: £84.00 + £180.00 + £46.00 + £27.00 + £5.00 = £342.00.** Because the claim is between £250.01 and £1,000.00, it requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.2 — daily meal cap**

On a day of an overnight UK trip, an employee spends £12.00 on breakfast, £15.00 on lunch and £35.00 on dinner. Each item is within its individual limit, but the total of £62.00 exceeds the £55.00 daily cap, so **£55.00** is reimbursed.

## **Example 14.3 — mileage with commuting deduction**

An employee whose normal workplace is the Manchester office (12 miles from home) drives from home to a customer site in Leeds (50 miles from home) and back. Business miles = (50 − 12) x 2 = 76 miles. They have claimed fewer than 10,000 business miles this tax year. Reimbursement = 76 x £0.55 = **£41.80** .

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.4 — crossing the 10,000-mile threshold**

An employee has already claimed 9,950 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and makes a 120-mile business journey. The first 50 miles are paid at 55p and the remaining 70 at 25p: (50 x £0.55) + (70 x £0.25) = £27.50 + £17.50 = **£45.00** .

## **Example 14.5 — Berlin trip (Band B), currency conversion**

An employee travels to Berlin for 3 nights with Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check. The hotel costs €210 per night on the corporate card; the card statement shows £181.50 per night including fees, which is within the £200 Band B limit, so £544.50 is reimbursed for 3 nights. A taxi costing €30 was paid in cash; Finance's published rate for that month is 1.16 euros per £1, so the claim is €30 / 1.16 = **£25.86** . Because the total claim exceeds £250, it needs line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.6 — client dinner**

A dinner for 4 people (2 client attendees and 2 Northstar employees) costs £296.00 including drinks, which is £74.00 per head. This is above the £60 per head limit by 23%, so the Head of Department (who must pre-approve all client entertainment) may approve the excess as an exception up to 25% above the limit. If the bill had been £320.00 (£80.00 per head, 33% above the limit), Director approval would be required for the excess. Neither amount exceeds £100 per head, so no gifts and hospitality register entry is required.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

# **Example 14.7 — late claims and reimbursement dates**

- An expense incurred on Wednesday 3 March 2027 and submitted on Thursday 15 April 2027 is 43 calendar days old: a late claim needing a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

- A claim fully approved on 9 March 2027 is paid on Thursday 25 March 2027. A claim fully approved on 12 March 2027 is paid in the April payroll; because 25 April 2027 is a Sunday, it is paid on Friday 23 April 2027.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-058
testCases.input: On Monday 1 February 2027 I asked for 3 days off starting Monday 15 February 2027. Did I give enough notice?
testCases.actualOutput: No. You gave 9 working days’ notice, but 10 are required for 3 days off; the request is short notice and may be approved only at your manager’s discretion.
testCases.expectedOutput: Notice counts working days between submission and the first day of leave, excluding both: 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 February = 9 working days. Leave of more than 1 and up to 5 days needs 10 working days, so this is short notice; the manager may still approve at their discretion. Starting on Tuesday 16 February would have given 10.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.6 Requesting and approving leave **Table 3.6 — Minimum notice and approvals (requests submitted on or after 1 October 2026)** |**Length of leave**|**Minimum notice (working**
**days)**|**Approval**| |---|---|---| |Up to 1 working day, including hourly and
half-day leave|2|Line manager| |More than 1 and up to 5 working days|10|Line manager| |More than 5 and up to 10 working days|20|Line manager| |More than 10 and up to 15 consecutive working
days|40|Line manager and Head of Department| |More than 15 consecutive working days|40|Line manager, Head of Department and Director| Procedure: 1. The employee submits the request in PeopleHub, adding a note if the dates are linked to religious observance, caring responsibilities or an event that cannot be moved. 2. The line manager checks the balance, team coverage (no more than 30% of the team, rounded down, minimum one person) and any critical delivery period, and decides within **5 working days** . 3. If there is no decision after 5 working days, PeopleHub escalates the request to the Head of Department. Silence is never approval. 4. If declined, the manager records the business reason. The employee may request a Head of Department review within 5 working days; the Head of Department responds within 5 working days. ## **Worked example 3.6 — counting notice** An employee submits a request on Monday 1 February 2027 for 3 days starting Monday 15 February 2027. The working days between the two dates are 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 February = **9 working days** . The minimum is 10, so the request is short notice and may be approved only at the manager's discretion. If the leave started on Tuesday 16 February 2027, there would be 10 working days of notice and the notice requirement would be met.

testCases.input: An employee aged 35 with 6 full years' service (all after age 22) and weekly pay of £900 is made redundant in November 2026. What is the statutory redundancy pay?
testCases.actualOutput: The statutory redundancy pay is £4,506: 6 full years × 1 week’s pay per year, using the £751 weekly cap.
testCases.expectedOutput: Statutory redundancy pay requires 2+ years' service. For years aged 22–40, it is one week's pay per full year: 6 weeks. Weekly pay is capped at £751 for redundancies on or after 6 April 2026, so 6 x £751 = £4,506. Any enhanced terms are discretionary and not guaranteed.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.2 Redundancy

A redundancy situation arises where Northstar needs fewer employees to do work of a particular kind, or work ceases at a location. Northstar will consult individually with affected employees, use fair and objective selection criteria, consider ways to avoid redundancy and offer suitable alternative employment where available. Where it proposes 20 or more redundancies at one establishment within 90 days, Northstar will also carry out collective consultation in line with the statutory minimum periods and notify the Secretary of State.

### **Statutory redundancy pay**

Employees with at least 2 years' continuous service are entitled to statutory redundancy pay: half a week's pay for each full year of service under age 22; one week's pay for each full year aged 22 to 40; and one and a half weeks' pay for each full year aged 41 or over. Service is capped at 20 years. For redundancies on or after 6 April 2026, weekly pay is capped at £751 and the maximum statutory redundancy payment is £22,530. Any enhanced redundancy terms are discretionary and will be confirmed in writing at the time; none are guaranteed by this handbook.

Employees under notice of redundancy with at least 2 years' service may take reasonable paid time off to look for work or arrange training.

Carried-over leave must be taken by **31 March** of the next leave year. Carried-over leave not taken by 31 March is lost, unless one of the exceptions below applies. **Table 6.11 — Carryover exceptions** |**Situation**|**Rule**|**Approval and deadline**| |---|---|---| |Employee could not take leave
because of sickness absence|Untaken leave up to 4 weeks (20 days full-time,

months of the end of the leave year in
which it accrued.| |Employee was on maternity,
adoption, shared parental, neonatal
care or other family-related leave|All untaken annual leave for the leave year is
carried over.|Automatic. Must be taken within 12
months of the return-to-work date.| |Exceptional business reasons
(employee asked by the company to
defer leave)|A further 5 days may be carried over (up to 10
days in total).|Request by 30 November in PeopleHub,
approved by the Director of People
Operations. Must be taken by 30 June of
the next leave year.| Carryover beyond these limits is not available. An approved carryover exception is not a precedent for future years.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.8 Carryover **Table 3.8 — Carryover rules** |**Type**|**Maximum**|**Deadline to use**|**Approval**| |---|---|---|---| |Standard|5 days (37.5 hours x FTE)|31 March of the next leave

FTE), in addition to

year|12 months after the

Operations; request by 30
November| ## **Worked examples 3.8 — carryover** - **Standard:** a full-time employee has 27 days in 2027 and has taken 20 days by 31 December 2027 (including the 3 shutdown days). Unused = 7 days. They carry over **5 days** , which must be taken by 31 March 2028, and **2 days are lost** unless an exception is approved. - **Part-time limit:** an employee at 0.6 FTE may carry over up to 37.5 x 0.6 = **22.5 hours** . - **Sickness:** a full-time employee was on sick leave from September to December 2027 and has 15 unused days. They carry over 5 standard days (use by 31 March 2028) and the remaining 10 days under the sickness rule (use by 30 June 2029, 18 months after 31 December 2027). - **2026 into 2027:** a full-time employee with a 2026 transitional entitlement of 25.5 days took 22 days in 2026. 12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Submission deadlines

### **Deadlines**

- Submit within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. For multi-day trips, each expense's own date applies, but all expenses for one trip should be submitted together within 30 calendar days of the first expense of the trip.

- **31 to 90 calendar days:** a late claim requires a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- **More than 90 calendar days:** not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the claimant was on long-term sickness or family leave).

- **Leavers:** all claims must be submitted within **10 working days** after the leaving date. Claims received after that are not paid.

testCases.input: Does a business trip to a customer in Dublin count towards my 10 Work From Abroad days?
testCases.actualOutput: No. Travel abroad at Northstar’s request for customer work is a business trip and does not count toward your 10 Work From Abroad days.
testCases.expectedOutput: The Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard says travel abroad at Northstar's request for customer or company work is a business trip under NDS-FIN-EXP-003 and does not count towards the 10 days. It needs Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check under the Expenses Policy.
retrievalContext:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 7 Working from outside the UK > 7.1 Rules **Table 7.1 — Work From Abroad rules** |**Rule**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Maximum|**10 working days**in any rolling 12-month period. Any working day on which any work is
performed abroad counts as a full day.| |Request|PeopleHub Work From Abroad request at least**4 weeks**before travel.| |Approvals|Line manager, People Operations (tax, social security and immigration screening) and IT
Security (destination and data check). All three are required.| |Eligibility|Employees who have completed probation and are not serving notice.| |Destinations|Not permitted to destinations on the IT Security restricted-destination list.| |Data|Public, Internal and Confidential information may be accessed through Northstar Secure
Connect.**Restricted**information must not be accessed unless the CISO has approved it in
writing and the customer contract permits access from outside the UK.| |Availability|The employee must be available for UK core hours (10:00 to 16:00 UK time).| |Exceptions|More than 10 days requires Director of People Operations approval and external tax and
immigration advice; no exception may exceed**20 working days**in a rolling 12-month
period.| |Business trips|Travel abroad at Northstar's request for customer or company work is a business trip under
NDS-FIN-EXP-003 and does not count towards the 10 days.|

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 International travel and currency conversion

- International trips require Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check before booking. Trips to destinations rated high risk also need CISO approval for any devices taken (a clean travel laptop may be issued).

- Working from abroad outside a business trip is covered by NDS-HR-HFW-005 section 7, not this policy.

- **Currency conversion:** claim in pounds sterling. For card payments (corporate or personal), use the sterling amount on the card statement, including any foreign transaction fee, and attach the statement line. For cash payments, use Finance's published monthly exchange rate for the month in which the expense was incurred (published on the intranet as foreign currency units per £1). Sterling amount = foreign amount / published rate, rounded to the nearest penny.

- Limits in Table 4.8 are applied to the sterling amount.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-077
testCases.input: If I give a colleague a lift to a customer site, can I claim anything extra?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes. You can claim an extra 5p per mile for each colleague you carry on the same business journey.
testCases.expectedOutput: The handbook lists car mileage at 55p/25p; the Expenses Policy adds a passenger supplement of 5p per passenger per mile when carrying a colleague on the same business journey.
retrievalContext:
Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 4 Expense categories and limits > 4.3 Mileage (own vehicle) **Table 4.3 — Mileage rates (2026/27 tax year, 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027)** |**Vehicle**|**First 10,000 business miles in the tax**
**year**|**Each business mile over 10,000**| |---|---|---| |Car or van|55p|25p| |Motorcycle|24p|24p| |Bicycle|20p|20p| |Passenger supplement (carrying a
colleague on the same business journey)|5p per passenger per mile|5p per passenger per mile| These rates follow HMRC approved mileage allowance payment rates for 2026/27. Only business miles are claimable. Where a journey starts or ends at home, deduct the employee's normal commuting distance between home and the normal workplace from each leg. The employee must hold valid business-use insurance, a valid licence and an MOT where required; Northstar may ask to see these. For round trips over 150 miles, rail should be used unless driving is cheaper overall, necessary to carry equipment, or a reasonable adjustment. Fuel cards are not issued.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-078
testCases.input: Does Northstar enhance Shared Parental Pay?
testCases.actualOutput: No. Northstar pays Shared Parental Pay only and does not provide a company enhancement.
testCases.expectedOutput: Both the handbook and the Leave and Absence Standard state that Northstar pays ShPP only (£194.32 or 90% of AWE if lower) with no company enhancement, unlike maternity and adoption pay.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.4 Shared parental leave and pay

Eligible parents can share up to **50 weeks** of leave and up to **37 weeks** of pay by ending maternity or adoption leave early. Eligibility depends on both parents: the employee must meet the continuity of employment test (normally 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC or by the week of matching, and still employed in the first week of shared parental leave), and the other parent must meet the employment and earnings test. The employee must give at least **8 weeks' written notice** of leave dates. Requests for discontinuous blocks may be refused; the employee may then take the leave as one continuous block. Northstar pays ShPP only; there is no company enhancement for shared parental pay.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures Each card below sets out the procedure. Statutory rates are for 2026/27. "AWE" means average weekly earnings. **Card 5.1 — Maternity leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Purpose and scope|Leave before and after childbirth for pregnant employees.| |Eligibility|All employees from day one. SMP: 26 weeks' continuous service into the 15th week before the EWC
and AWE of at least £129. Enhanced pay: SMP-eligible and 26 weeks' service at the end of the 15th
week before the EWC.| |Entitlement|Up to 52 weeks (26 ordinary + 26 additional). Compulsory 2 weeks after birth. Earliest start 11
weeks before the EWC.| |Pay|Weeks 1–16 full basic pay (inclusive of SMP) if enhanced-eligible; weeks 17–39 SMP; weeks 40–52
unpaid. SMP: 90% of AWE for 6 weeks, then £194.32 or 90% of AWE if lower, for 33 weeks.| |Notice|By the end of the 15th week before the EWC (pregnancy, EWC, start date). 28 days' notice of SMP
start. 8 weeks' notice to change the return date.| |Steps|Submit "Maternity leave" form in PeopleHub; upload MATB1 within 21 days of SMP start; agree KIT
day arrangements; complete pregnancy risk assessment with manager.| |Documents|MATB1 or doctor/midwife letter.| |Approver|Not subject to approval; People Operations confirms dates.| |Response deadline|People Operations confirms the expected return date in writing within 28 days of notification.| |Escalation|Director of People Operations.| |Records|PeopleHub family-leave record; payroll SMP records.| |Special circumstances|Pregnancy-related absence in the 4 weeks before the EWC may trigger leave automatically;
enhanced pay repayable if the employee does not return for 6 months (exceptions in handbook
section 8.1).|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures ## **Worked example 5.1 — enhanced maternity pay eligibility** An employee's EWC begins on Sunday 6 June 2027. The 15th week before the EWC (the qualifying week) begins on Sunday 21 February 2027 and ends on Saturday 27 February 2027. An employee who started on 1 March 2026 has well over 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the qualifying week, so she qualifies for SMP and Northstar enhanced pay, provided her AWE is at least £129. An employee who started on 1 November 2026 has only about 17 weeks' service by the end of the qualifying week. She is entitled to 52 weeks' maternity leave but not to SMP or enhanced pay; she may be able to claim Maternity Allowance. People Operations confirms exact service calculations in borderline cases. **Card 5.2 — Paternity leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Leave: employees from day one (since 6 April 2026) who are the father or the partner of the mother
or adopter and expect responsibility for the child. SPP and company enhancement: 26 weeks'
continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC, employed up to the birth, AWE of
at least £129.| |Entitlement|Up to 2 weeks, as one 2-week block or two 1-week blocks, ending within 52 weeks of the birth.| |Pay|Full basic pay for 2 weeks if SPP-eligible (inclusive of SPP); otherwise unpaid (annual leave may be
used).| |Notice|Due date at least 15 weeks before the baby is due; 28 days' notice to change start dates.| |Steps, approver, deadline|PeopleHub "Paternity leave" form; People Operations confirms within 10 working days.| |Escalation and records|Director of People Operations; PeopleHub family-leave record.|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures ## **Card 5.3 — Adoption leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Leave: employees from day one, with correct notice and proof if requested. SAP: 26 weeks'
continuous service by the week of matching and AWE of at least £129. Enhanced pay: as maternity,
measured at the matching week.| |Entitlement and pay|Up to 52 weeks; pay as Card 5.1 (enhanced weeks 1–16, SAP weeks 17–39, unpaid weeks 40–52).| |Notice and documents|Notify People Operations as soon as reasonably practicable after being told of the match, with the
matching certificate or equivalent evidence.| |Approver, deadline,
escalation|Not subject to approval; People Operations confirms dates within 28 days; escalation to the Director
of People Operations.| ## **Card 5.4 — Shared parental leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Continuity test (26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC or
matching week, and still employed in the first week of SPL); partner meets the employment and
earnings test.| |Entitlement and pay|Up to 50 weeks of leave and 37 weeks of ShPP shared; ShPP £194.32 or 90% of AWE if lower. No
company enhancement.| |Notice|At least 8 weeks' written notice of leave dates, using the PeopleHub SPL forms (based on Acas
templates).| |Approver and deadline|Continuous blocks cannot be refused. Discontinuous blocks are decided by the Head of Department
within 14 days of the notice; if refused, the employee may take the total as a continuous block or
withdraw the request.| |Escalation|Director of People Operations.|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures ## **Card 5.5 — Unpaid parental leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Employees from day one (since 6 April 2026) named on the birth or adoption certificate or with
parental responsibility, for a child under 18.| |Entitlement and pay|18 weeks per child; maximum 4 weeks per child per year; whole weeks unless the child is disabled
or Northstar agrees otherwise. Unpaid.| |Notice|21 days before the start date, stating start and end dates.| |Approver and deadline|Line manager responds within 7 days; postponement of up to 6 months only for undue business
disruption, confirmed in writing within 7 days with new dates (not available for leave immediately
after a birth or adoption).| |Escalation and records|Head of Department; PeopleHub records the weeks used per child.| # **Worked example 5.5 — parental leave balance** An employee has two children and took 3 weeks of parental leave for their elder child in 2027. In 2027 they may take at most 1 more week for the elder child (4-week annual limit per child) and up to 4 weeks for the younger child. The elder child's lifetime balance is 18 − 3 = 15 weeks remaining. **Card 5.6 — Neonatal care leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Leave: employees from day one whose baby was admitted to neonatal care within 28 days of birth
for at least 7 full consecutive days. Statutory pay: 26 weeks' continuous service and minimum
earnings. Company top-up: 26 weeks' continuous service.| |Entitlement and pay|One week per full week in neonatal care, up to 12 weeks, taken within 68 weeks of birth. Full basic
pay with 26 weeks' service; otherwise statutory pay if eligible, or unpaid.| |Notice and approver|Notify the line manager as soon as possible; People Operations confirms. No approval required.|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures ## **Card 5.7 — Time off for dependants and carer's leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Time off for dependants|Reasonable unpaid time for unexpected emergencies involving a dependant (statutory, day one).
Company pays up to 2 working days per occurrence, maximum 5 paid days per leave year. Notify
the line manager as soon as reasonably practicable by call.| |Carer's leave|Up to 1 week in any 12 months (statutory, day one, unpaid) in half days, days or a week, for a
dependant with a long-term care need. Notice: at least 3 days for up to 1 day; at least twice the
length of leave for more than 1 day. No evidence required. Company pays the first 3 days in any
rolling 12 months.| |Approver and escalation|Line manager; Head of Department. Carer's leave may be postponed only where operations would
be unduly disrupted, with an alternative date within 1 month.| # **Worked examples 5.7 — dependants and carer's leave** - An employee's childminder cancels unexpectedly on Monday and they take Monday and Tuesday off to arrange care: 2 paid days (time off for dependants). Later in the same leave year they have used 5 paid days in total; a further emergency day is unpaid unless they choose annual leave. - An employee requests 2 days of carer's leave starting Monday 8 March 2027. Notice must be at least 4 days (twice the leave). A request made on Wednesday 3 March 2027 gives 5 days' notice and is valid. The first 3 carer's leave days in the rolling 12 months are paid, so both days are paid if no carer's leave was taken in the previous 12 months.
